name: Mardi Gras Hotel & Casino

sources.observed: Official front and pool gallery inspected; ochre stucco, bronze mansard, iron rails, cream decks, blue pool tile and terracotta coping.
November 2021 front panorama: three storeys, exterior corridors, arched openings, deep canopy, slender columns and stone bases.
Aerial inspected: two parallel wings, west connector, separate courtyard building, pool toward eastern half; image capture date unspecified.
Official pool image inspected: blue tile, terracotta coping, scalloped outline, cream deck, blue loungers and steel handrails.
Official exterior corridor detail inspected: rough stucco arch and iron balustrade.
Official site-6 and site-4 images inspected; machine closeups only, no reliable room layout. Interior remains deferred.

Evening courtyard photograph inspected: exposed straight stair with intermediate landing beside taller pavilion, upper terrace rails and connections toward guest corridors. Capture date unknown; historic Wynn skyline.
Daylight photograph independently shows exposed stair beside pavilion and upper terrace; image date unknown, older furnishings. Used for permanent circulation only.

Official first/second/third floor PDFs all downloaded from linked legacy host and visually inspected. Schematic guest room numbering, west reception/casino/restaurant, central New Orleans Pavilion and Baton Rouge North/South, second-floor guest laundry. No stair symbols or dimensioned circulation; repeated central diagram on all floors cannot establish pavilion elevations.

Official photograph visually inspected 2026-10-28: beige walls, chair rail, white plantation shutters, folding partition/ceiling tracks, recessed rectangular lights, brown/gold patterned carpet, round green cloth tables and covered chairs. Supports finishes, not surveyed ceiling height or precise room orientation.

Official buffet photograph visually inspected: matching patterned carpet, beige walls/shutters, round pale tables, teal upholstered chairs and buffet carts. Exact placement within pavilion versus restaurant not established; do not merge layouts based on finishes alone.

Garden photo visually inspected 2026-10-28: oval hedge/patio, white tables/chairs, turquoise parasols, lawn, curved paths and two mature broadleaf trees. Capture date unknown. Aerial inspected separately places garden east of pool before eastern pavilion; small service structure between pool/garden still absent from authored pass.

Overhead satellite view visually inspected 2026-10-28 with panel collapsed. Confirms pool then garden then eastern pavilion sequence, oval garden seating island and planted edges. Copyright2026 is not capture date.

Official close-up reinspected2026-10-28: raised narrow standing seams, bronze swept central sign face rising from canopy and pale raised letters. Corrected original floating rectangular sign approximation; exact profile, 0.62m seam pitch and text size remain inferred. Garden photograph separately shows shingled long guest wings; removed metal seam extension from those areas before final install.

2026-10-28 closer aerial, eastward pan: spa is small shadowed basin south/southwest of brown L-shaped service roof, NOT tree circle on north lawn. Used central pavilion/east pavilion surveyed footprints as relative anchors; pool ends before service roof and oval garden lies west of eastern pavilion. Image capture date unspecified.

Historical property description calls terrace second-story, but lists old Best Western branding and obsolete room equipment. Does not establish surveyed height; conflicts with ambiguous photographic floor alignment. No new height claimed.

Photo-supported two-flight exposed stair, intermediate and upper landings, upper terrace and corridor rail openings, taller central pavilion and east glazing.

Original oval courtyard garden with clipped hedge openings, paved public path, lawn, white seating/turquoise parasols and two branched leaf-mesh trees, fitted to aerial and garden photograph.

Raised standing seams/rolled edge on west bronze roof; taller swept sign face above canopy with side returns and pale letters. Long guest-wing roof uses a separate non-metal finish supported by garden photograph; shingle microdetail remains pending.

Coordinated spa/service/garden refit: southern spa, original brown L-shaped utility shell with roof trim/vent, garden moved west with north–south path, shorter pool enclosure and revised gate/furniture exclusions.

Public New Orleans and divided Baton Rouge meeting rooms from official 103x38ft plan, west double entry and three side exits, walkable partition doorways, ceiling/trim/shutters, original woven carpet/table fabrics and sparse event seating. Separate optimized streamed interior with fixed shared lighting.

meetingInteriorPlan.implementationNotes: Official plan re-inspected during courtyard pass: west main double entry, New Orleans/Baton Rouge partition after58ft from west end, longitudinal Baton Rouge N/S divider. Side exits near west end of Baton Rouge and one south New Orleans exit. Use local mapped shell with explicit thickness and keep boardroom unlocated. Ceiling height can only be photo-fitted and must be labeled estimated; no need to invent casino/private rooms. Preserve independently unresolved terrace elevation.
